gemini-3-7-flash.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash is now a compatibility endpoint
gemini-3-7-flash.text: Google deprecated Gemini 3.7 Flash on October 8, 2026. It is no longer selectable in Google AI Studio; requests using gemini-3.7-flash are routed to gemini-3.8-flash. Update model IDs and validate function calls, reasoning controls, output schemas and effective costs against the replacement. Earlier 3.7 specifications, benchmarks and prices describe the original release, not an independently selectable model today.

The advantage is that 3.7 remains fully supported, has the same published introductory Standard token prices as 3.8, and can be a sensible efficiency-first target when a workflow does not benefit from 3.8's heavier long-horizon reasoning behavior.

gemini-3-8-flash.title: Migration from Gemini 3.7 Flash and 2.5 Pro
gemini-3-8-flash.text: Since October 8, 2026, requests to gemini-3.7-flash route to Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google announced that gemini-2.5-pro requests will route to gemini-3.8-flash and use its rates beginning December 1, 2026. Change the model ID before that date and review breaking changes including thought signatures, thinking_level instead of thinking_budget, sampling controls and prefilled turns. Google made the Computer Use tool generally available on October 30 across GenerateContent and Interactions. For newer coding workflows, also evaluate Gemini 4 Hydrogen (GA November 12); do not assume it replaces every 3.8 endpoint.
sources: Google API release notes — October 8, October 30, November 2 and November 12
replacements: Gemini 3.8 Flash is Google’s recommended model for computer use, with the capability currently marked preview on the model page.
Gemini 3.8 Flash supports the Computer Use tool; Google announced its general availability across GenerateContent and Interactions on October 30, 2026.

gemini-3-6-flash.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash migration and endpoint routing
gemini-3-6-flash.text: Google announced on October 8, 2026 that gemini-3.5-flash is deprecated and calls to that endpoint are automatically routed to gemini-3.6-flash. Use gemini-3.6-flash explicitly (or assess Gemini 3.8 Flash) and retest token usage, function calls and generation settings rather than treating legacy benchmark results as measurements of the routed endpoint. Google's lifecycle schedule lists no announced shutdown date for gemini-3.6-flash.

gemini-3-5-flash-lite.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash migration deadline: December 1, 2026
gemini-3-5-flash-lite.text: Google announced on November 2 that gemini-2.5-flash is deprecated and will route to gemini-3.5-flash-lite at the latter model's rates from December 1, 2026. The change is scheduled, not yet in effect on the date of this review. Update the model string and validate function calls, thought signatures, thinking_level, sampling controls and prefilled turns. This notice does not deprecate the separate gemini-2.5-flash-lite endpoint.

gemini-embedding-001.title: Plan the transition to Gemini Embedding 2
gemini-embedding-001.text: Google's deprecation schedule lists May 14, 2028 as the earliest shutdown date for gemini-embedding-001, with gemini-embedding-2 as the recommended successor. This is a planning date, not an announcement that the older endpoint is already offline. Embedding 001 and Embedding 2 use different vector spaces: regenerate stored vectors and query vectors with the replacement and validate retrieval quality before switching production traffic.

gemini-embedding-2.title: Preview-to-GA migration does not require re-indexing
gemini-embedding-2.text: On November 6, 2026, Google deprecated gemini-embedding-2-preview and began routing requests to gemini-embedding-2 at the stable model's rates. Google states that the preview and GA endpoints share the API schema and embedding space, so changing the model string does not require regenerating the vector index. This exception does not apply to a migration from Gemini Embedding 001, which uses a different embedding space.

gemini-3-5-transcribe.title: Voice-driven editing added on November 17, 2026
gemini-3-5-transcribe.text: Google added voice editing to both gemini-3.5-transcribe and gemini-3.5-transcribe-live on November 17. Spoken instructions can edit, rewrite or format dictated text or an existing source_text value. The non-streaming and Live endpoints remain distinct integrations. For verbatim captions, evaluate transcription-only and editing workflows separately so spoken edit instructions are not mistaken for literal transcript content.

claude-haiku-4-5.title: Text watermark and current API lifecycle
claude-haiku-4-5.text: Anthropic announced on November 16, 2026 that Haiku 4.5 generated text carries its text watermark on supported platforms. Non-default temperature, top_p or top_k settings may result in text without the watermark. The watermark announcement does not change the API's token price or context specification. Anthropic's lifecycle table still lists claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 as active; October 15, 2026 was the earliest possible retirement date, not an actual retirement.

voxtral-mini-transcribe-2.title: Deprecated V2 endpoint and explicit V3 aliases
voxtral-mini-transcribe-2.text: Mistral lists the February 2026 batch transcription model as deprecated and recommends Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 for new integrations. The version-pinned replacement is voxtral-mini-transcribe-3-0; the migration guide also names voxtral-mini-transcribe-3 and voxtral-mini-transcribe-latest as V3 aliases. Do not assume the old voxtral-mini-latest alias is interchangeable. Recheck response schemas and timing requirements before switching. V2 prices and capabilities are historical reference values; confirm retirement and continued access with Mistral.
replacements: Mistral documents the model as GA Premier v26.02 and optimized for transcription purposes only.
Lifecycle rechecked 2026-11-24: Mistral originally released the model as Premier v26.02 for transcription only; it is now deprecated for new hosted integrations.

voxtral-mini-transcribe-realtime.title: Deprecated hosted V2 realtime model; migrate to Realtime 3
voxtral-mini-transcribe-realtime.text: Mistral's current directory marks the hosted February 2026 realtime model deprecated. For new integrations the documented replacement is voxtral-mini-transcribe-realtime-3-0 (Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3). Revalidate WebSocket event handling, turn detection, streaming delay and transcript assembly against the V3 documentation. The API lifecycle notice does not itself revoke the Apache 2.0 licence of the separately released V2 open weights, and historic V2 prices should not be assumed to apply to V3.

claude-fable-5-1.title: Fable 5.2 successor and migration requirements
claude-fable-5-1.text: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026. Both generations retain 1M context and 128K maximum output with adaptive thinking. Fable 5.2 Standard rates are $8 input and $40 output per million tokens versus Fable 5.1's $10 and $50; these are successor rates, not a change to 5.1 billing. Before migrating, review enforced prefix checks for replayed thinking blocks, computer_toolset_20260801, advisor compatibility and the 30-day retention requirement. Fable 5.2 Fast mode is a separate $16/$80 tier. Fable 5.1 remains active; the September 1, 2027 retirement floor is not a shutdown announcement.

claude-mythos-5-1.title: Mythos 5.2 successor for verified organizations
claude-mythos-5-1.text: The November 9 release introduced Claude Mythos 5.2 for organizations approved through Anthropic verification programs. It offers 1M context, 128K maximum output and adaptive thinking; its published $8/$40 per million input/output tokens are distinct from Mythos 5.1's $10/$50 rates. Migration requires strict preserved-thinking prefix checks, newer computer-use toolset compatibility and account-specific access. Both generations require 30-day retention unless Anthropic expressly authorizes an exception. The release does not make Mythos publicly accessible.

gpt-live-1.title: GPT-Live-1.1, standby, SIP and native decisions
gpt-live-1.text: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live-1.1 on November 19, 2026 with improved multilingual pronunciation, accent consistency and transcription. Both Live-1 and Live-1.1 WebRTC sessions can use standby to pause inference during inactivity. Outbound SIP calling became available to all organizations November 2; prompt-to-voice launched October 16 (voice creation is free, speech uses regular Live billing), along with additional localized voices. Native GPT-6 Luna Decisions delegation was added October 15. Retest voice interruptions and delegation when changing the model ID; backend model and tool charges remain separate from session billing.

gpt-6-luna.title: Decisions API GA and background processing
gpt-6-luna.text: OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available on October 22 using gpt-6-luna. POST /v1/decisions accepts up to 400 typed questions, structured input_json, question-level images and shared-prefix prompt caching. Its input rate is $0.10 per million uncached tokens; output tokens are not billed on this endpoint. Cache charges and applicable regional or long-context premiums remain separate. This is not the ordinary Responses API output price. On November 17, OpenAI also introduced optional two-hour and eight-hour background completion windows in public beta, at 30% and 40% lower token rates than Standard.
sources: OpenAI API changelog — October 22 and November 17

gpt-6-1-sol.title: Ultrafast service tier and Healthcare configuration
gpt-6-1-sol.text: OpenAI enabled service_tier=ultrafast for GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API on October 8, with separate rate limits and support for global, US and EU processing. Persistent WebSockets are recommended for tool-heavy applications. On November 24 OpenAI introduced gpt-6.1-sol-healthcare, a distinct Responses API configuration using a medical-source search index when web search is used. GPT-6.2 Sol was released November 17 and is now the newer general-purpose Sol option. These service tiers and model configurations should not be conflated with the original GPT-6.1 Sol Standard rates or benchmark results.
sources: OpenAI API changelog — October 8 and November 24

gpt-image-2-5-sunburst.title: Markup-guided editing and GPT-Image-2.6
gpt-image-2-5-sunburst.text: OpenAI added markup-guided editing for supported GPT-Image-2.5 and 2.6 models in November. Use POST /v1/images/edits with the original image, a transparent PNG markup overlay matching the first image's dimensions, and a prompt describing the intended change. Regional edits through the Responses API instead use a mask. The new GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst adds complexity controls, SVG and animated GIF generation; those 2.6-specific capabilities must not be assumed for 2.5. The current image-generation guide recommends 2.6 for new integrations. Preserve 2.5-specific prices and evaluate actual editing fidelity before switching.

gpt-image-2-5-flare.title: Markup-guided edits and the next Flare generation
gpt-image-2-5-flare.text: The updated Image API supports markup-guided editing on supported GPT-Image-2.5 and 2.6 models. Submit the original image and a matching transparent PNG annotation layer to POST /v1/images/edits, with instructions in the prompt. The Responses API uses masks for regional editing. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare is the newer model and introduces complexity settings, SVG and animated GIF generation; these are not automatically available on 2.5 Flare. OpenAI recommends the 2.6 family for new integrations. Benchmark generation latency, editing quality and actual billed token usage rather than assuming equal cost across generations.

mistral-large-2512.title: Mistral Large 3 API deprecation and Apache 2.0 weights
mistral-large-2512.text: The current Mistral Large 3 card marks the hosted model deprecated and recommends Large 4 for new integrations. The original model remains a 675B-total, 41B-active multimodal MoE with 256K context and Apache 2.0 weights. The official card distinguishes hosted lifecycle from downloadable weights and lists an approximate 1,800–450 GB GPU RAM range from BF16 to FP4; this is a model-card estimate, not total memory for every serving configuration. The earlier $0.50/$1.50 token prices describe the historical hosted reference, not guaranteed future API availability.

mistral-large-4.title: General availability, open weights and revised Standard rates
mistral-large-4.text: Mistral published Large 4 weights on October 29, 2026. The November 5 model card lists GA and $0.70 input, $0.07 cached input, $2.10 output per million tokens. The older October rates remain historical; the GA card provides the dated evidence boundary, not an independently confirmed billing-transition date. The model now always reasons: low, medium and high (default), with none removed. The official 1T-A52B checkpoint uses Mistral Ecosystem Open Weight License, not Apache 2.0. Mistral reports 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 28.3% at preview, and 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index; these are vendor-reported or attributed results, not new SXF measurements.

gemini-3-8-live.title: Live API migration and per-query grounding billing
gemini-3-8-live.text: Google lists November 17, 2026 for retirement of the 3.1 Flash Live preview, with gemini-3.8-live as its replacement. Use the stable model ID and retest interruptions, audio format, session resumption and tool handling. Standard modality rates remain $0.75/$4.50 per million text tokens and $3/$12 per million audio tokens. Search grounding is metered by individual search queries rather than user turns; its allowance is shared across eligible Gemini models.

gemini-3-8-live-extended-thinking.title: Extended Thinking: asynchronous session contract
gemini-3-8-live-extended-thinking.text: Google documents low, medium and high thinking levels but not MINIMAL; proactive audio cannot be disabled. A completed audio turn does not prove that background processing is finished: wait for interaction_status IDLE and keep receiving tool calls and audio while IN_PROGRESS. Calls must be non-blocking, and client content with turn_complete=true interrupts active generation. The shared Live rate card includes thinking tokens in output charges.

The November 24 pricing review found no separate cached-input rate for this SKU. Earlier published cache figures are retained in the historical ledger, not used as current billing assumptions.

gpt-realtime-2-1-mini.title: Realtime Mini: migration from older speech endpoints
gpt-realtime-2-1-mini.text: OpenAI's October 1 notice schedules tts-1, tts-1-hd and gpt-4o-mini-tts for shutdown on January 6, 2027, recommending GPT-Realtime-2.1 Mini. Older gpt-realtime-mini and gpt-4o-mini-realtime are scheduled for January 20. These migration paths do not guarantee identical voice or endpoint behavior. The mini model's 128,000 context and 32,000 max output limits, and $0.60/$0.06/$2.40 text-token rates are unchanged.

gpt-transcribe.title: Transcription migration: recordings and committed realtime turns
gpt-transcribe.text: OpenAI's August 26 notice schedules Whisper and older GPT-4o transcription models for shutdown on February 26, 2027. GPT-Transcribe supports recorded files, file-streaming transcripts and completed Realtime turns over WebSocket; use GPT-Live-Transcribe for live incremental captions. The model card still lists $0.0045 per audio minute. Test context hints, response formats and timestamp or diarization requirements before switching.

gpt-live-transcribe.title: Realtime transcription: preserve workflow semantics during migration
gpt-live-transcribe.text: For the February 26, 2027 retirement of older transcription models, choose GPT-Live-Transcribe for incremental live captions and GPT-Transcribe for recordings or committed turns. OpenAI lists $0.017 per live audio minute and $0.0045 per minute for the file/committed-turn model. Before switching, validate supported context and language hints, item-based delta reconciliation and required response shapes. File-streaming is not equivalent to low-latency microphone transcription.

gpt-realtime-translate.title: Realtime translation: dedicated endpoint and graceful closure
gpt-realtime-translate.text: OpenAI announced retirement of /v1/audio/translations on February 26, 2027. Use /v1/realtime/translations with gpt-realtime-translate, configure the target language in session.update, and stream audio continuously. At the end send session.close, then wait for session.closed to avoid losing queued audio or transcript deltas. Use one session per source stream and target language. The documented 16,000 context, 2,000 max output and $0.034/audio minute remain unchanged.

embed-v4-0.title: Embed 4: vector dimensions and migration boundary
embed-v4-0.text: Embed 4 remains listed for text and multimodal retrieval. Its supported vector sizes are 256, 512, 1024 and 1536 (default), with a 128K context. Embed 5 is the newer family; its Pro/Fast interoperability does not establish compatibility with Embed 4. For a version upgrade, build a separate index and evaluate retrieval before switching traffic. Cohere's public pricing page describes dedicated Model Vault instance rates, not a verified per-token Standard rate for this API.

embed-v5-0-pro.title: Embed 5 Pro: shared vector space and November availability
embed-v5-0-pro.text: Cohere recommends Pro for corpus indexing and quality-sensitive retrieval, with Fast available for query-time embedding in the same vector space. Match output_dimension and representation across index and query. Both variants accept text and images, support 128K context and return vectors of 256, 512, 768, 1024, 1536 or 2048 dimensions (2048 default). Cohere announced OpenRouter availability on November 4, 2026 under cohere/embed-5-pro. Direct API, managed deployment and partner billing are separate; no direct numeric Standard token rate is asserted.

embed-v5-0-fast.title: Embed 5 Fast: query-time retrieval and November availability
embed-v5-0-fast.text: Cohere recommends indexing with Pro and embedding interactive queries with Fast. The models share a vector space; use identical dimensions and output type. Fast supports 128K context and the same six vector lengths (256–2048), with float, int8 and binary representations. OpenRouter added cohere/embed-5-fast on November 4, 2026. Compare partner rates separately from direct API or Model Vault; the direct Standard price is not confirmed.

rerank-4-pro.title: Rerank 4 Pro is a previous-generation reranker
rerank-4-pro.text: Cohere released Rerank 5 on October 21, 2026 and recommends rerank-v5.0-pro for new quality-sensitive workloads. Rerank 4 Pro remains listed, not announced as retired in the model overview. Migration changes the ranking model, not stored corpus embeddings: send documents to the newer endpoint and retest ranking quality and thresholds. Rerank 5 adds Context Focus and calibrated relevance scores; do not assume these features exist in Rerank 4. The 32K context covers query plus document for each inference; search-unit billing is separate from LLM output tokens.

rerank-4-fast.title: Rerank 4 Fast: migration to Rerank 5 Fast
rerank-4-fast.text: Rerank 5 Fast is Cohere's recommended successor for high-throughput reranking. Cohere reports improved quality even versus 4 Pro, but this is provider evidence rather than an SXF benchmark. Change the model ID to rerank-v5.0-fast and compare latency, relevance and thresholds on your own candidate set. There is no vector index migration solely for a reranker change. The earlier 4 Fast endpoint is still listed; no shutdown date or numeric direct search-unit rate was confirmed.

parse-v5-0.title: Parse 5: layout-aware output and deployment options
parse-v5-0.text: Cohere's release identifies Parse as a 2.3B-parameter multimodal parser. Its output can represent reading order, tables, page boundaries and visual locations, including Markdown/HTML and bounding boxes. The API reference describes a blocks output with ordered page regions. Use the Parse API rather than a chat completion; production systems should validate table structure, page ordering and missing regions. Cohere lists Microsoft Foundry, SageMaker and Model Vault options. No public direct per-page numeric rate was confirmed; the full model card could not be retrieved for this review.

north-mini-code-1-0.title: North Mini Code: open weights versus hosted evaluation
north-mini-code-1-0.text: The provider lists 30B total and 3B active MoE parameters, 256K context, 64K maximum output and Apache 2.0 weights. Chat V2, Chat V1 and Chat Completions are documented; Cohere offers evaluation keys subject to limits and production via Model Vault. The 3B active parameter count is not total storage or VRAM. Size the actual checkpoint, runtime and KV cache for local use. Treat tool execution as a harness capability with controlled permissions, not an unrestricted model action.
replacements: Available through Chat V2 API and as Apache 2.0 open weights.

command-a-reasoning.title: Command A Reasoning: serving guidance and newer Command A+
command-a-reasoning.text: Cohere still lists the August 2025 reasoning endpoint as Live, with 256K context, 32K output and a June 1, 2024 knowledge cutoff. Its model card reports 111B parameters and support for 23 languages. Cohere recommends four H100 GPUs for production deployment and four A100s for evaluation; these are provider configurations, not universal hardware requirements. Command A+ is a newer MoE alternative with different limits, so compare workloads rather than assuming equivalent behavior. Rate-limited free API access is not a paid production tariff. The overview identifies this endpoint as text input; confirm any generic image-capability badges against the specific endpoint before enabling vision.

codestral.title: Codestral: current pricing and FIM endpoint
codestral.text: Mistral's current model overview and price table retain Codestral as the code-completion specialist. Standard rates per million tokens remain $0.30 input, $0.03 cached input and $0.90 output. Use the fill-in-the-middle endpoint with a prefix and suffix when completing an existing file; ordinary chat generation is a different integration. Keep the dated identifier codestral-2508 for reproducible evaluations and verify aliases before migrating. The old model-card URL could not be opened directly, so the existing 128K context and unpublished output limit are retained rather than reverified.

codestral-embed.title: Codestral Embed: vector shape and native billing
codestral-embed.text: Mistral's model card lists GA Premier v25.05, 8K context, and Embeddings and Batch endpoints. The code embedding guide describes output_dimension and output_dtype controls, up to 3072 dimensions. The API alias is codestral-embed; keep dimension and representation consistent between indexed code and query vectors. Standard pricing is $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.015 for cached input, with no generative output charge. Embedding dimension is not a text output-token cap.

mistral-small-4.title: Mistral Small 4: open hybrid architecture and serving costs
mistral-small-4.text: Mistral Small 4 remains GA under Apache 2.0. Its mixture-of-experts architecture has 119B total parameters and 6.5B active parameters; active parameters do not determine the full checkpoint size. The model card lists 256K context, chat completions, function calling, structured outputs, predicted outputs, document Q&A and Batch. The Standard rate card lists $0.15 input, $0.015 cached input and $0.60 output per million tokens. No independent output cap is published in the model card; do not treat the context limit as an output allowance.

mistral-ocr-4-1.title: OCR 4.1: page billing, annotations and cached-rate disclosure
mistral-ocr-4-1.text: OCR 4.1 remains a GA Premier hosted API. The model card distinguishes $4 per 1,000 standard pages and $5 per 1,000 annotated pages; the current Standard pricing table also displays $0.40 per 1,000 cached input pages. Do not treat cached pricing as an automatic discount or add both page categories to every request. The SXF calculator continues to estimate uncached standard or annotated processing separately; the catalog retains its base per-page meter. Use /v1/ocr for layout blocks, paragraph bounding boxes, structural labels and confidence scores. Validate extracted tables and uncertain blocks before downstream use.

ministral-14b-2512.title: Ministral 3 14B: distinguish API from downloadable variants
ministral-14b-2512.text: Mistral lists the 14B dense model as GA with a 256K context and separate Apache 2.0 base, instruct and reasoning weights. The dated API identifier is ministral-14b-2512; a separate reasoning checkpoint is not a guarantee of hosted reasoning_effort support. The provider's weight table estimates roughly 93 GB at BF16 and 24 GB at FP4 for its documented context configuration, not minimum weight-only VRAM. Standard API rates are $0.20 input, $0.02 cached input and $0.20 output per million tokens. Function calling, structured outputs, document Q&A and Batch are documented.

ministral-8b-2512.title: Ministral 3 8B: edge deployment and documented API features
ministral-8b-2512.text: The 8B dense model remains listed in the active portfolio with 256K context. Mistral provides Apache 2.0 base, instruct and reasoning checkpoints with vision support; the dated hosted endpoint is ministral-8b-2512. The weight table estimates approximately 67 GB BF16 to 17 GB FP4 GPU RAM for its documented configuration, not a universal minimum. Standard API rates are $0.15 input, $0.015 cached input and $0.15 output per million tokens. Use the appropriate checkpoint locally; hosted function calling, structured outputs and Batch are documented separately.

ministral-3b-2512.title: Ministral 3 3B: local footprint and inference limits
ministral-3b-2512.text: The 3B dense model remains listed with a 256K context and text/image understanding. Apache 2.0 base, instruct and reasoning checkpoints are distinct from the hosted ministral-3b-2512 endpoint. Mistral's weight table estimates roughly 43 GB BF16 to 11 GB FP4 GPU RAM for its documented configuration; shorter contexts and other runtimes may differ. The Standard API rate is $0.10 input, $0.01 cached input and $0.10 output per million tokens. Document Q&A, structured outputs, function calling and Batch are available; an independent maximum output limit remains unpublished.

mistral-embed.title: Mistral Embed: cached-input price and safe indexing
mistral-embed.text: Mistral's current rate table lists $0.10 per million ordinary input tokens and $0.01 per million cached input tokens, without a separate generated-output fee. The provider has not supplied an effective-start date for the cached rate in the reviewed table; SXF records the newly verified figure without asserting when it first took effect. The model remains GA Premier with 8K context and Embeddings and Batch endpoints. The existing SXF estimator assumes uncached inputs, so its calculations remain valid. Keep the same model and vector representation for indexing and querying; a text embedding is not a generated-text output.

shieldstral-1-0.title: Shieldstral 1.0: self-hosted policy classification
shieldstral-1-0.text: The model card still labels Shieldstral 1.0 Public Preview, Apache 2.0, with 3.8B total and active parameters and a 32K context. It evaluates natural-language policy questions against text or image content, returning a yes/no classification for prompt/response moderation, refusal detection and safety filtering. Mistral's latest price table explicitly lists self-hosting rather than a hosted per-token API price. Costs therefore depend on local infrastructure; the model is distinct from Mistral Moderation 2. Treat classification as a policy signal, not a guarantee of safety.

gemini-3-1-pro-preview.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview: availability and complete cost tiers
gemini-3-1-pro-preview.text: Google's lifecycle table has no announced shutdown date for gemini-3.1-pro-preview; the endpoint remains Preview, not GA. The separate gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools endpoint prioritizes custom tools in agent workflows and uses the same pricing. Standard per-million rates for prompts up to 200K tokens are $2 input, $0.20 cached input and $12 output including thinking; above 200K they are $4, $0.40 and $18. Cache storage is $4.50 per million token-hours. The model card confirms 1,048,576 input and 65,536 output tokens and support for Batch, Flex and Priority; Live API and image generation are not supported. Search grounding is separately billed per query beyond the shared allowance.

gemini-3-1-flash-image.title: Nano Banana 2: stable endpoint and recommended successor

The card lists Batch support but no Flex or Priority; the reviewed price table shows only Standard, so confirm other serving-tier rates before use.
